about: Every connection that leaves the machine: what it is for, which direction data flows, the protocol, the secrets in .env, the verb that uses it, the automation flag that lets it run unattended, and the readiness integration that records a person's verification.
authority: docs/OPERATIONS.md section 2, src/orchestration/run/readiness.ts (INTEGRATIONS), the env names the code reads, package.json
secretsRule: Secrets live in the gitignored .env and .secrets/, never in the repo, a journal or an event. The runner hands each child only its verb's family (envFor in steps.ts) and strips every secret from an agent's environment.

readinessStates.implemented: the code exists and its tests pass (INTEGRATIONS in readiness.ts)
readinessStates.verified: a person exercised it against the real service and recorded the evidence (readiness.json, via npm run run -- verified)
readinessStates.enabled: configured to run unattended (automation.json); every flag is off by default

services.name: YouTube Data API v3
services.direction: out (upload, metadata, captions, thumbnail, visibility) and in (sync, verify)
services.protocol: HTTPS REST, resumable upload, OAuth 2.0 refresh token
secrets: YOUTUBE_CHANNEL_ID_<KEY> or YOUTUBE_CHANNEL_ID (the channel an upload must land on)
verbs: npm run publish -- auth | upload | push | go-live | sync | verify
guards: upload sends only private; refuses before any byte unless the authenticated channel is the commission's
a lost upload session stops and asks a person rather than uploading twice
only a person goes live (automated: refused); a live video is never replaced
a fixture topic's output goes unlisted at most, never public

services.name: YouTube (public pages, through the watcher)
services.direction: in (video metadata and transcripts for claims)
services.protocol: the watcher CLI in the sibling checkout (../retire-sim/watcher or WATCHER_DIR) fetches; evidence -- search lists hits

services.name: Study and document search
services.protocol: HTTPS fetch; evidence -- fetch-doc is the only way a document enters the corpus
services.note: the only two verbs a collect agent may run; some hosts block bots and need a headless fallback

services.name: Approval mailbox (SMTP out, IMAP in)
services.direction: out (halt mails, digest, draft and release requests, proposal batch, correction requests, launch mail) and in (replies: OK, OK at <when>, CHANGES:, PAID OK, APPROVE <slug>, REJECT <slug>)
services.protocol: SMTP 465 (nodemailer), IMAP 993 (imapflow, mailparser); every Message-ID generated by the caller; request ids signed with APPROVAL_SECRET
verbs: npm run run -- tick (outbox flush, inbox poll)
guards: the outbox records a mail before the send: at-least-once with a stable id
a reply is applied once, by thread and by request id; a reply on a decided request is answered, never applied
OK alone (or OK at <when>) is the only release approval; OK followed by anything is a clarification

services.name: Azure AI Speech (release voice)
services.protocol: microsoft-cognitiveservices-speech-sdk, in a worker process (npm run tts-azure)
services.note: final re-narrates the accepted draft's words in the neural voice; the draft used edge-tts
services.enabledBy: runs inside a story run after the draft is accepted

services.name: Microsoft Edge TTS (draft voice)
services.protocol: edge_tts.py through VK_PYTHON; no key; throttled by the service

services.name: OpenAI (optional TTS/STT)
verbs: npm run video -- narrate when VK_TTS_PROVIDER names it
services.note: an alternative provider, not the default; the release voice is Azure

services.name: X API (posts)
services.protocol: HTTPS, OAuth 1.0a user context per institution
verbs: npm run social -- show | compose | post
guards: optional per institution: no keys is 'not configured', journaled, never a halt
an intent is recorded in social.json before the call and the id after; never twice for one textSha
posted only after the launch probe confirms the deploy, when enabled.social and launch.social.video say so

services.name: Cloudflare Workers (static assets of the Astro build)
services.direction: out (git push triggers the host's own deploy) and in (links -- live probes the public URL)
services.protocol: wrangler.jsonc: build npm run build, assets ./dist; the host deploys on push
secrets: none in .env; the host holds its own
guards: the launch job stages only the story's folder, the topic's top-level files and the site outputs; deploy-timeout after launch.deployTimeoutMinutes, written once

services.name: GitHub (origin, Actions, Pages mirror)
services.direction: out (push) and the Actions run: npm ci, validate, audit, browser tests on three engines, deploy the Pages mirror under /video-knowledge/ with DEPLOY_TARGET=pages
secrets: the git credential the person configured
verbs: git push (the launch job or a person)

services.name: Claude Code CLI (every agent step)
services.direction: out (brief, role grant, budget cap) and in (the artifact written, usage and cost in the attempt record)
services.protocol: claude -p with per-role permission rules; the model alias per role from automation.json agents.models; effort from agents.effort
secrets: the claude CLI signed in on PATH; no key in .env
verbs: every prompt step of npm run run -- story | topic | discover | maintain
guards: per-role Edit rules, no shell for content roles, no web unless the role says
the tree guard reverts writes outside the role's files and typechecks a graphics agent's components before a child loads them
the attempt is the unit of spend: perAgent cap, perRun, perTopic, perWeek checks; budget.json is the gate
services.enabledBy: enabled.work for unattended runs; by hand always
services.cost: a research run cost 46 to 61 USD a topic in the two real runs

services.name: The watcher library (sibling repo retire-sim/watcher)
services.direction: local: the store's writer runs its CLI from the checkout
services.protocol: node src/modules/evidence/watcher.mjs runs ../retire-sim/watcher/src/cli.ts (or WATCHER_DIR); .claude/skills/watcher/SKILL.md is a verbatim copy of its contract

services.name: Windows scheduled tasks (the tick and the work plane)
services.direction: the OS starts npm run run -- tick (short, every schedule.tickMinutes) and npm run run -- work (one long job, then exit)
services.protocol: npm run run -- schedule --print prints the commands; a person creates the tasks, never a run
services.note: scheduled-tasks is implemented: false in readiness.ts: creating the tasks is the person's act

services.name: Strudel bench (generative music)
services.direction: local: a headless browser renders compositions to WAV; npm run music -- import brings them in
services.protocol: STRUDEL_BENCH names the bench; WAVs are never committed; licence.cleared is a person's hand edit
verbs: npm run music -- cues | import | render | show

attachesToRule: attachesTo names the object(s) in objects.json the service reads or writes; the admin System model draws the connection there.
